season.evidence: 149 of 193 logged summits fall in May-Jul (59/59/31); ascent reports agree the sweet spot is snow-firmed spring and early summer, with Aug-Oct a loose-scree slog and winter needing a snowmobile approach.

track.why: Logged Willow Creek to SW Ridge on 2023-06-22: Willow Creek drainage to the SW/west ridge saddle and the summit block is our West Ridge standard line. Summited, tops out 4 m from our summit pin, round trip from the SR-20 pullout (start/end 134 m and 121 m from our current pin; about 100 m from the WTA-confirmed pullout).

pins.name: SR-20 pullout (Silver Star / Willow Creek approach)
pins.evidence: Our route text starts at a SR-20 pullout about 3.5 mi east of Washington Pass (~4,320 ft) and drops to Early Winters Creek. Nine harvested tracks start in a cluster at 48.551,-120.6309 (334 m from our pin at 48.548) at 4,300-4,311 ft per the loggers' own start-trailhead stats: the Silver Star climbers' pullout. WTA places that trailhead at the first pullout past the Cutthroat Creek turnout near the milepost 165 marker, at 48.5500,-120.6306 (about 100 m from the track cluster).
pins.confirmedBy: https://www.wta.org/go-hiking/hikes/silver-star-mountain-okanogan (GPS 48.5500, -120.6306; first pullout after the Cutthroat Creek turnout, near mile marker 165)

facts.text: In mid-May, rime and verglas on the summit block can make the first low moves far harder than in dry conditions.
Boulders on the upper slope shift easily underfoot; keep the party close together and avoid climbing beneath each other.
A bear was met on the lower approach in late June; make noise in the brush.
Pack at least one cam for the lower chimney; slings alone give poor protection there.
Bring rock shoes for the chimney and the summit slab; boots make both moves awkward.
Carry a long sling and a ring or two for the summit bolt, which had no rappel hardware in late May.
Pull the rope from the left (south) rappel station of the lower pitch; the rope can lodge in a crack above the other line.

Stay left of the waterfall cliff band in the Willow Creek valley; angling right of the creek runs into cliffs. A higher log crossing a few hundred feet upstream of the lowest one keeps your feet drier on Early Winters Creek.
Mid-to-late May: snow is continuous from roughly 6,500-6,800 ft and firm in the morning, good with crampons to about 7,200 ft, but it turns punchy by afternoon.
Late June: the basin is still snow-filled up to the ridge slope, leaving only 50-100 ft of loose scree at the top; an axe and crampons are useful there.
When afternoon snow turns punchy in May, descend the narrow gully east of your ascent gully rather than the one you climbed.

notes: Single route on the peak, so every West/SW Ridge/Willow Creek/Standard ascent is the same line (runner-ups marked unsure only because their mechanical start check fails on the pin, not on route identity). Our trailhead pin sits about 220 m south of the Silver Star pullout where nine of ten tracks start; the proposed move would let most good tracks pass the 300 m rule. Our summit pin is fine (within 12 m of Peakbagger). Stored season Apr-Oct is wider than the evidence; proposed May-Jul.
